sections.heading: C2 — Space management
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Space management

FACT_ID: sec11-R01 | anchor: A01
Give pedestrians extra room, especially children who may enter your path without warning. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-R02 | anchor: A01
Do not share the lane with a pedestrian or bicyclist; wait until passing in the adjoining lane is safe. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-R03 | anchor: A01
When facing hazards on both sides, steer a middle path unless one hazard warrants extra space on its side. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-R04 | anchor: A01
When possible, separate hazards by letting oncoming traffic pass before overtaking a bicycle. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-R05 | anchor: A01
The handbook advises a gap of about four seconds when changing lanes, entering traffic or joining a merging lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-R06 | anchor: A01
Moving into the middle of a four-second gap leaves a two-second interval ahead and behind in the handbook’s merging example. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-R07 | anchor: A01
Do not merge into a gap too small to leave a safe space cushion. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-R08 | anchor: A01
Cross multiple lanes by changing one lane at a time. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-R09 | anchor: A01
To cross traffic, choose a gap large enough to clear the entire roadway without stopping. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-R10 | anchor: A01
To enter traffic, leave space to complete the turn and accelerate to traffic speed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-R11 | anchor: A01
Stop halfway across traffic only if a median can hold the entire vehicle without any part projecting into traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-R12 | anchor: A01
Before turning left, make sure no vehicle or pedestrian blocks the intended path. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-R13 | anchor: A01
Even with a green signal, do not enter an intersection when vehicles block the way through. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-R14 | anchor: A01
Blocking an intersection can result in a citation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-R15 | anchor: A01
Do not rely only on an approaching vehicle’s turn signal before pulling out; wait for it actually to begin turning, then proceed only if safe. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-R16 | anchor: A01
A motorcycle’s turn signal may remain on because it often does not cancel automatically. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-R17 | anchor: A01
Pass only where signs or markings allow it and there is enough room to do so safely. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-R18 | anchor: A01
As a general rule, pass one vehicle at a time rather than assuming space to pass several. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-R19 | anchor: A01
The handbook’s 55-mile-per-hour passing example uses about ten seconds of passing time and an oncoming-traffic gap of that duration. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-R20 | anchor: A02
If both vehicles travel at 55 miles per hour toward each other, each covers over 800 feet in ten seconds, requiring more than 1,600 feet of combined space in the handbook example. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-R21 | anchor: A02
If uncertain that a distant oncoming vehicle leaves enough room, wait before passing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-R22 | anchor: A02
For passing near a hill or curve, the handbook calls for sightlines of at least one-third of a mile, or about ten seconds ahead. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-R23 | anchor: A02
Do not begin a pass within one-third of a mile of a hill or curve that blocks the view. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-R24 | anchor: A02
Passing near intersections, railroad crossings or shopping entrances is dangerous because traffic can enter or cross the road. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-R25 | anchor: A02
Before passing, check for pedestrians, bicyclists, narrow roadway, ice, potholes or other obstacles that could force vehicles into your lane. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-R26 | anchor: A02
Do not pass without space to return to your driving lane, and do not assume another driver will make room. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-R27 | anchor: A02
Before returning after a pass, leave enough room; seeing both headlights of the passed vehicle in the rearview mirror is the handbook’s return cue. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-R28 | anchor: A02
The handbook requires a rear slow-moving emblem on animal-drawn vehicles and most farm vehicles and construction equipment. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-R29 | anchor: A02
Approach a slow-moving vehicle cautiously and pass only when safe. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-R30 | anchor: A02
Give right of way to an animal being led, ridden or driven. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-R31 | anchor: A02
Slow near an animal or horse-drawn vehicle and stop if it approaches you or crosses your path. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-R32 | anchor: A02
When passing an animal moving your way, allow ample room and use a reasonable speed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-R33 | anchor: A02
Do not honk or make loud noises near animals. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-R34 | anchor: A02
If an animal you are passing appears frightened, pull aside and stop. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-R35 | anchor: A02
Proceed past an animal only when safe, and stop if its rider or driver signals you to stop. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-R36 | anchor: A03
Horseback riders are governed and protected by road rules and must ride single file near the right edge or on a usable right shoulder, lane or path. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec11-R37 | anchor: A03
Use due care, reasonable speed and a reasonable separation when approaching a horse being ridden or led along the road. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec11-R38 | anchor: A03
Sounding the horn while approaching or passing a horse is illegal. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec11-R39 | anchor: A03
Give extra room to drivers whose views are blocked at entrances or who are backing into traffic or parking spaces. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec11-R40 | anchor: A03
Allow extra room for drivers with obscured windows and pedestrians whose umbrella or hat blocks their sight. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec11-R41 | anchor: A03
Give extra room or exercise extra caution when another road user appears distracted. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec11-R42 | anchor: A03
Treat unfamiliar, unexplained slowing or sign-searching drivers as potentially confused and leave room. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec11-R43 | anchor: A03
If someone passes without enough room, slow to help that driver return safely rather than worsening the mistake. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec11-R44 | anchor: A03
If another driver must change lanes suddenly, slow to allow a merge. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0078]

corpus_stability.reason: This is a bounded snapshot of the issuer-linked Montana handbook. Its revision conflict is explicitly held as debt; there is no evidence in the supplied source of multiple substantive rewrites per year. Currency of individual changeable provisions is not inferred from this assessment.
